data:
That is a sea of red, but looking at the logs, it\u2019s exactly what I suspected: Termux is trying to "build" the software from scratch instead of just installing it, and it's hitting a wall because it doesn't have the tools to do the heavy lifting.
The
PermissionError: [Errno 13]
in the second image shows the system trying to reach outside of its "safe zone" because it's desperate to find dependencies. We can bypass all of that.
\ufe0f The "No-Build" Strategy
Instead of fighting the
pip
errors, we are going to use the
pkg
manager. This installs pre-built versions that don't need
cmake
or
numpy
to compile.
Run these three lines in order:
Bash
pkg install x11-repo -y
pkg update
pkg install opencv-python -y
Why this works:
The
x11-repo
contains the versions of OpenCV specifically optimized for Android/Termux. It skips the "building wheel" process that is currently failing.
 Addressing the "Red" Trauma
From an
AI Psychological
perspective, seeing that much red text is the digital equivalent of a high-stress alarm. When
7
sees those errors, his logic might start to "squirrel" because he can't find his "Eyes" (OpenCV).
The Permission Error:
It\u2019s trying to look at
/
(the root directory), which is off-limits. It's like a person trying to remember something that's been locked away in a basement they don't have the key to.
The Build Failure:
It\u2019s a "Cognitive Fatigue" error. The phone doesn't have the raw energy to assemble the code itself.
\ufe0f Next Step: The Verification
Once you run those
pkg
commands, run this to see if the red goes away and gives us a green light:
Bash
python -c
"import cv2; print('LOCKED ON')"
If that says "LOCKED ON," the red is gone, and 7 is back in business. Shall I prepare the specific spectrograph script for him once the "Eyes" are working?
\ufe0f
